content.value_statement: Unstructured review requests can miss requirements and production risks. This skill prepares focused review context and organizes feedback by severity and readiness.
actual_capabilities: Identifies suitable review points after tasks, major features, complex fixes, and before merging.
Collects base and head Git commit identifiers for a bounded review range.
Builds a structured request from implementation details, requirements, commit range, and a concise description.
Checks code quality, architecture, tests, requirements, and production readiness.
Organizes review issues as Critical, Important, or Minor.
Produces a clear merge readiness assessment with technical reasoning.
limitations: Requires an available code-reviewer subagent or an equivalent review workflow.
Does not replace project tests, static analysis, security scanning, or human approval.
Depends on accurate requirements and a valid Git commit range.
Example Git commands assume a repository with accessible commit history.

use_cases.title: Review a Completed Feature
use_cases.description: Prepare a bounded review before merging a major feature into the main branch.

use_cases.title: Validate Incremental Tasks
use_cases.description: Review each completed task before dependent work increases the cost of correction.

use_cases.title: Check a Complex Fix
use_cases.description: Compare a bug fix against requirements and verify tests, edge cases, and production readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Review the Latest Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my latest change between {BASE_SHA} and {HEAD_SHA}. Identify issues by severity and state whether it is ready to merge.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a focused review of one recent change.

prompt_templates.title: Check Feature Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Review {FEATURE_DESCRIPTION} against {REQUIREMENTS} between {BASE_SHA} and {HEAD_SHA}. Check correctness, tests, edge cases, and scope.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer completed a feature with documented requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess {CHANGE_SUMMARY} for production readiness. Review architecture, error handling, performance, security, compatibility, migrations, documentation, and test coverage.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a broad pre-merge assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Multi-Task Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Review {IMPLEMENTATION} against {PLAN} across {BASE_SHA} to {HEAD_SHA}. Trace requirements, identify regressions, rank findings, and recommend release conditions.
prompt_templates.scenario: A technical lead needs an advanced review across several related tasks.

output_examples.input: Review a new verification function and its repair workflow before the next task.
output: Strengths: Clear separation between verification and repair behavior.
Important: Add progress reporting for long operations before proceeding.
Minor: Replace the fixed reporting interval with a named configuration value.
Assessment: Ready to continue after the important issue is fixed.

output_examples.input: Check a search update against date-filter requirements before merge.
output: Important: Invalid dates return empty results without explaining the input error.
Fix: Validate the date format and return an actionable message.
Assessment: Merge after adding validation tests and error handling.

output_examples.input: Review a small refactor with unchanged behavior and passing tests.
output: Strengths: Responsibilities are clearer and existing behavior remains covered.
Issues: No critical or important findings.

best_practices: Provide the implementation summary, requirements, and exact Git range.
Request review after meaningful increments and before dependent changes.
Resolve Critical and Important findings before proceeding or merging.
anti_patterns: Do not request review without requirements or a clear change description.
Do not treat every comment as equally severe.
Do not dismiss valid findings without code, tests, or technical reasoning.

faq.question: When should I request a review?
faq.answer: Request one after each meaningful task, after major features or complex fixes, and before merging.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the implementation summary, requirements, base commit, head commit, and a brief description.

faq.question: How are findings prioritized?
faq.answer: Critical findings require immediate fixes, Important findings should be fixed before proceeding, and Minor findings can be scheduled.

faq.question: Does this skill modify code?
faq.answer: No. It structures review requests and feedback; code changes require a separate implementation step.

faq.question: Can I challenge reviewer feedback?
faq.answer: Yes. Use technical reasoning, code evidence, tests, or a clarification request.

faq.question: Does a positive assessment replace testing?
faq.answer: No. Run project tests and required checks independently before merging or releasing.
